extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of classical political philosophy; general readers interested in forms of government
extracted.subtask_description: A close, discursive account of the nature, origins, internal characteristics, and defects of regimes (oligarchy, democracy, tyranny) and the corresponding character-types of individuals who embody them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honor determines cultivation
rubrics_metrics.description: That which is honoured is cultivated, and that which has no honour is neglected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The social valuation of persons and pursuits directs what is developed or abandoned in a State; honouring the rich leads to neglect of virtue and the virtuous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property qualification for citizenship
rubrics_metrics.description: A law fixes a sum of money as the qualification of citizenship; those whose property falls below the amount fixed have no share in government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formal property qualification is the legal mechanism by which oligarchy excludes the poor and institutionalizes rule by the wealthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule by wealth over competence
rubrics_metrics.description: Choosing rulers or officials according to property rather than skill (e.g., choosing pilots by property) leads to incompetence and disaster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative anti-pattern: selecting leaders on wealth rather than ability results in 'shipwreck' — governance failures due to misplaced qualifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Class division and factionalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Oligarchy divides the State into two factions, the poor and the rich, who live together yet conspire against one another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such inevitable division undermines unity and stability; factional antagonism is a central defect of oligarchy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military weakness and tax aversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Oligarchies are incapable of carrying on any war effectively: they either arm the multitude and fear them, or have too few to fight; their fondness for money makes them unwilling to pay taxes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Political economy (stinginess) compromises defense and public finance, weakening the state's security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplex occupations / lack of specialization
rubrics_metrics.description: Under oligarchy the same persons have too many callings — husbandmen, tradesmen, warriors — leading to poor performance in each.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A lack of role specialization dilutes civic effectiveness and social function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alienated paupers within the polis
rubrics_metrics.description: A man may sell all he has and remain dwelling in the city as a pauper, neither trader nor artisan nor soldier — a helpless creature excluded from civic roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Property loss without civic status produces alienated individuals who are neither fully citizen nor productive member.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extreme inequality breeds crime
rubrics_metrics.description: Oligarchies feature both extremes of great wealth and utter poverty; where paupers exist, thieves, cut-purses, robbers of temples, and malefactors arise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economic extremes correlate with social disorder; lack of education, ill-training, and bad constitutional arrangements contribute to criminality.

rubrics_metrics.name: False appearance of citizenship based on spending
rubrics_metrics.description: A spendthrift may appear to be a member of the ruling body when wealthy, but in truth he is neither ruler nor subject but only a spendthrift — a drone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wealth can produce mere appearances of civic status without the virtues or responsibilities of true citizenship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drones (stingless) and stinging drones — social parasites
rubrics_metrics.description: Some drones end as stingless paupers in old age, while stinging drones become the criminal class; drones are a plague to the city as to the hive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes types of social parasites and links them to decay: both idle consumers and predatory criminals harm the polity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education and constitution prevent crime
rubrics_metrics.description: The existence of criminals is to be attributed to want of education, ill-training, and an evil constitution of the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preventive remedy: cultivate education and proper constitutional arrangements to reduce criminality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oligarchical individual: valorisation of wealth and penurious character
rubrics_metrics.description: The oligarchical individual values wealth highly, is penurious and laborious, satisfies only necessary appetites, confines expenditure to them, and lacks cultivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Psychological profile linked to regime: miserly habits and avoidance of higher cultivation reproduce oligarchical social forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forced virtue vs. true virtue
rubrics_metrics.description: The oligarchical man coerces his bad passions by necessity and fear (trembling for possessions), not by reason; his enforced virtue is not genuine.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: apparent honesty deriving from fear of loss, not from cultivated moral understanding — precarious moral reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miser’s unfitness for honourable competition
rubrics_metrics.description: The miser will not spend his resources in contests for glory and so fights with only a small part of his resources, commonly losing prizes and saving money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avarice undermines participation in civic and aristocratic contests, producing inferior civic virtues and reputations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oligarchy breeds revolution by creating paupers and resentment
rubrics_metrics.description: Through increasing extravagance among rulers and the spread of carelessness, men of good family may be reduced to beggary and remain in the city eager for revolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rulers’ neglect and profit motives (buying up estates) exacerbate social resentment that can lead to upheaval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy remedy: voluntary contracts to limit exploitative money-making
rubrics_metrics.description: A general rule that every one shall enter into voluntary contracts at his own risk will lessen scandalous money-making and the evils under discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposed institutional reform to reduce predatory financial practices: rely on voluntary, risk-borne contracting to curb exploitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy’s origin: poor conquer and equalize power
rubrics_metrics.description: Democracy comes into being after the poor have conquered their opponents, slaughtering some and banishing others, and give an equal share of freedom and power; magistrates are commonly elected by lot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes constitutional mechanism and social basis for democracy: mass victory and selection by lot rather than property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy: liberty, variety, and equality of unequals
rubrics_metrics.description: In democracy the city is full of freedom and frankness; a man may say and do what he likes; there will be the greatest variety of human natures and equality dispensed to equals and unequals alike.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Democracy’s virtues: freedom and pluralism; its risks: indiscriminate equality that neglects merit and cultivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic neglect of cultivation and statesmanship
rubrics_metrics.description: Democracy tramples fine notions of cultivation (the upbringing in beauty and study that makes a statesman) and promotes to honour any one who professes to be the people’s friend, regardless of true worth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-pattern: popular favour replaces long-term education and formation of statesmen, undermining governance quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessary vs unnecessary pleasures
rubrics_metrics.description: Necessary pleasures are those we cannot get rid of and are beneficial; unnecessary pleasures are those which can be controlled, do no good, and often harm body and soul.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral taxonomy used to distinguish oligarchical (necessary-only-focused) and democratic (indulgent) characters; educational training should curb unnecessary desires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic individual: motley life and lack of order
rubrics_metrics.description: The democratic man lives from day to day, indulging the appetite of the hour — motley and manifold, changing pursuits, having neither law nor order in life; he despises none of his pleasures and encourages them all equally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Character profile of democracy’s subject: instability, libertinism, and equality of desires rather than hierarchy of goods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excessive liberty leads to tyranny
rubrics_metrics.description: The excess of liberty in democracy, when magnified, often causes a reaction in the opposite direction and passes into excess of slavery — tyranny arises from democracy when freedom is unbounded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General political principle: unbridled freedom can provoke concentrated domination as its corrective or consequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drones as the plague of cities — keep them away
rubrics_metrics.description: Idle spendthrifts (drones), courageous leaders and timid followers, are the plagues of every city; a good lawgiver should, like a wise bee-master, keep them at a distance or have their cells cut out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Normative recommendation: proactively exclude or remove parasitic social elements to preserve civic health.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democracy’s social triad: drones, wealthy orderly class, the people
rubrics_metrics.description: Democracy may be divided into three classes: drones (many intensified), the orderly wealthy class (most squeezable), and the working people who are the largest class but often need inducement to assemble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytic taxonomy of democratic social composition; highlights how drones extract from the wealthy and manipulate the people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Populist redistribution is corrupted by leaders
rubrics_metrics.description: Leaders who deprive the rich of their estates and distribute them among the people reserve the larger part for themselves, using informers to charge the rich with plotting and forcing them to defend themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes corruption mechanism in democratic redistributions: demagogues expropriate for followers while enriching themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pathway from protector to tyrant
rubrics_metrics.description: A protector of the people, with a mob at his disposal, by false accusation, murder, promises (abolition of debts, land partition), and then returning from exile with a bodyguard, becomes a tyrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence of political moves: popular champion → abuses of power → elimination of rivals → paramilitary guard → absolute tyranny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tyrant’s maintenance: wars, impoverishment, purging the good
rubrics_metrics.description: The tyrant stirs up wars to keep people needing a leader and to impoverish them by taxes; he must rid himself of valiant, high-minded, wise, or wealthy citizens and instead assemble paid satellites and freed slaves as a bodyguard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical tactics of tyranny: manufacture external threats, fiscal extraction, purge potential rivals, and build loyal, paid forces.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tyrant’s reversal of purgation (removing the better part)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike physicians who purge the worse and leave the better, the tyrant purges (eliminates) the better citizens and keeps the worse, reversing the healthy order of the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moral judgment on tyranny’s destructive logic: the polity becomes worse because its best elements are removed.
